label: late original-phase "t" input in sequences starting with q/z/l/digit
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.007% of steps). About 70% of activation mass is on the input token t at late original positions (orig_idx 5-8, usually the last or second-to-last token before <DEL>, in long sequences with L=8-9). Another roughly 10% is on the <DEL> step. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<5. Firing and magnitude depend strongly on sequence context: the first token is q (lift 15x), or less often z, l, or a digit, and q/z often appear early in the sequence. Preceding tokens like u, d, b raise the rate. Even with these conditions only about 8% of matching steps fire, so the gating context is not fully captured. The plain rule (t at orig_idx>=5) covers 70% of mass but has about 1% precision. There are also weak activations on other late tokens (v, y, w) and on <DEL>.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=q (+4.68), orig1=z (+4.32), orig2=z (+3.45), phase=0 & in_tok=t (+2.67), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=t (+2.67), orig0=l (+2.54). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.15), next_out=- (-2.52), prev_tok=z (-1.49), orig4=t (-1.32).
